title: MirrorWorks — Edge Onramp Partner Intro / Capacity Alignment
next_steps: Send partner integration brief and capacity questionnaire
Share SOC2 + connectivity and VPC onboarding docs
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with MirrorWorks infra team (week of Dec 21)
action_items: Maya Chen | Send integration brief + pricing ranges | 2026-12-14
Samir Patel | Prepare pilot workload checklist and target perf metrics | 2026-12-18
Diane Xu | Provide current peak token/sec and batch profiles | 2026-12-15
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and MirrorWorks to explore edge onramp partnership. Discussed MirrorWorks' distribution of GPU-enabled edge clusters, routing and multi-tenant resale model, security expectations (VPC, KMS), and high-level pilot scope. Agreed to exchange docs and schedule technical deep dive to run throughput benchmarks and validate KV cache sharing patterns.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing for partners
transcript:
00:00 Lena Ortiz: alright everyone we're live, thanks for making time
00:04 Maya Chen: great to meet you all, Maya from Redwood AE, joined by Samir and Olivia on the infra side
00:12 Rajiv Menon: morning, Rajiv here, quick timezone note I'm in IST so catching first half of the call, Tom will cover ops later
00:20 Maya Chen: perfect, we'll go through quick intros then a light set of discovery questions. goal is to see if a partner onramp makes sense and what a pilot would look like
00:35 Diane Xu: sounds good, we're keen to avoid reinventing the orchestration layer, MirrorWorks runs GPU clusters in 12 edge regions today, mostly A100 and a fleet of mixed GPU nodes
00:46 Samir Patel: when you say edge regions, are these customer-managed racks or your own co-lo footprint?
00:52 Diane Xu: mostly our colo, a handful of customer-prem racks in finance customers, so mixed tenancy. we do tenant isolation with strict VM boundaries, but networking is a bit bespoke per site
01:05 Maya Chen: high level — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. for partner models we typically provide routing policies and an SDK to integrate with partner orchestration. is MirrorWorks looking to resell Redwood hosted endpoints, or host Redwood runtime on your infra?
01:22 Lena Ortiz: intent is resale + optional private installs for strategic customers. we'd like to offer a managed inference product via our marketplace, but some customers will require private VPC or on-prem options
01:36 Olivia Park: ok. do you expect to run the Redwood runtime inside your clusters (private) or would you prefer proxying traffic to Redwood-hosted endpoints?
01:45 Rajiv Menon: probably both. for smaller customers we want to route to hosted for cost reasons, for bigger banks we need private with KMS integration and local residency
01:58 Diane Xu: also latency matters — many of our customers need sub-50ms token latencies for short chat flows, others are batch embedding workloads so throughput > latency
02:10 Samir Patel: that's a useful split. we typically recommend: hosted for low-friction cases; dedicated reserved for consistent throughput; private for data residency and KMS/HSM integration. in partner scenarios we can expose a routing layer so you can choose per-tenant policy
02:27 Lena Ortiz: licensing: are there reseller margins, or is it strictly pass-through pricing?
02:33 Maya Chen: we have partner pricing tiers — simple summary we'll send after — but for pilots we can do discounted reserved blocks. we'll include example math for margining in the brief
02:42 Tom Becker: ops question: how do you handle burst traffic that exceeds reserved capacity? we need to make sure we don't drop customer requests
02:50 Samir Patel: fallbacks — we allow policy-based fallback to compatible model variants and cross-region spill. autoscaling + burst pools are configurable, and we can set soft limits to avoid rejections. for peak bursts, could also route to lower-cost endpoints to avoid errors
03:08 Rajiv Menon: what about KV cache behavior when models are run across multiple nodes? we care about cold-start token overheads
03:14 Olivia Park: our runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching. for cross-node runs the cache isn't shared unless you use a coordinated cache layer. for many interactive flows we recommend pinning sessions to a node or using sticky routing to keep KV locality
03:30 Diane Xu: sometimes sticky routing isn't possible with our load balancer, can Redwood tolerate higher cold-start overheads?
03:36 Samir Patel: yes, there are tradeoffs. we can recommend quantization profiles and micro-batching to reduce per-token compute. we'll run bench of your workload to give more precise latency/cost curves
03:52 Lena Ortiz: security — SOC2 is table stakes. do you provide audit logs per-tenant and SSO for partner portals?
03:59 Maya Chen: yes to both. Redwood provides audit logs, token-level cost breakdowns, and RBAC; SSO (SAML/OIDC) is supported for partner console access. for private installs we integrate with customer KMS (or HSM) and provide audit export hooks
04:15 Tom Becker: encryption at rest — we must ensure keys never leave our zone for private deployments
04:20 Olivia Park: completely doable — we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. we'll document the pattern and expected network ports in the onboarding guide
04:30 Lena Ortiz: on the operational side, what metrics do you expose for partner billing and chargebacks?
04:36 Samir Patel: token accounting, per-request cost, per-model and per-route breakouts. the console also supports report exports for monthly billing reconciliation
04:46 Rajiv Menon: network egress. some of our customers are very sensitive to cross-region egress between EU and US; do you have regional isolation options?
04:54 Maya Chen: yes, we have regionalized endpoints and routing policies. for data residency we can ensure inference stays in region or run private control plane with an on-prem data plane if needed
05:07 Diane Xu: pilot idea: pick a single EU edge site, run a small chat demo and an embedding pipeline for 2k QPS sustained for 2 hours, measure latency P50/P95 and token cost. is that realistic?
05:20 Samir Patel: absolutely, we'd like sample payloads and sequence length distributions. also need to know batch sizes you prefer and whether KV sharing is required across requests
05:31 Lena Ortiz: we'll share anonymized traces and payload distribution. also want to discuss SLAs and support model if this becomes productized
05:40 Maya Chen: for pilots, we typically offer a support window with on-call SE coverage and weekly syncs. production SLAs are part of Dedicated/Private enterprise contracts
05:50 Tom Becker: curious about multi-tenant isolation — if we're reselling hosted endpoints, do you provide per-tenant rate limiting and quotas?
05:57 Olivia Park: yes, rate limits and quotas per API key, and per-route quotas. we also have usage analytics to detect noisy tenants
06:05 Rajiv Menon: any known limitations with certain open models or quantization levels on edge GPUs? we run a bunch of older Ampere and some H100s in our cloud
06:14 Samir Patel: older Ampere can work with INT8 and GPTQ-style quantization in many cases, but some models need kernel-level optimizations. we'll flag model compatibility in the catalog and can run a quick validation test on your hardware profile
06:28 Diane Xu: integration surface: do you provide container images or a binary bundle for private installs?
06:33 Maya Chen: we provide a containerized runtime and an installer that supports air-gapped and VPC deployments. we'll send an ops checklist for required ports, disk, and GPU drivers
06:44 Lena Ortiz: networking — our edge sites sometimes sit behind NAT and proprietary load balancers. anything special we need to change?
06:50 Olivia Park: there are patterns. for control plane connectivity we need outbound connectivity to Redwood control endpoints; for air-gapped we do an offline bundle. for data plane you can configure a reverse proxy to allow inbound traffic from your load balancer
07:05 Tom Becker: what's the expected onboarding time for a private site? internal SLA from Redwood?
07:10 Maya Chen: small private site can be 2-3 weeks (installer + validation + basic tests), larger takes longer. for partner resellers the first two pilots would be treated as onboarding onboarding and SE time is included in the pilot budget
07:24 Rajiv Menon: cost question — do you have example numbers for per-token compute on A100 vs H100? we need to model margin in our marketplace
07:32 Samir Patel: yes, we'll send a simplified cost matrix that shows token/sec costs by GPU type, sequence length, and quantization. it'll include memory limits and throughput sweet spots
07:44 Diane Xu: compliance: any experience with banking customers and their penetration testing cycles?
07:49 Maya Chen: we have customers in fintech; we can share SOC2 reports and past pen-test summaries where permitted. but for new bank customers, joint pen-tests are common and we support them via our security team
07:58 Lena Ortiz: good. procurement question: do you require an MSA for pilot?
08:03 Maya Chen: typically we have a short pilot SOW and standard partner MSA. we can keep the pilot paperwork lightweight
08:12 Tom Becker: okay, shifting toward pilot scope — what are minimal success criteria you want from MirrorWorks?
08:18 Samir Patel: from Redwood's perspective: reproducible P95 within target (e.g., <120ms for chat flows), consistent throughput for embedding pipelines (target QPS), and reliable KV locality behavior. also ability to integrate routing policies in your marketplace UI
08:33 Lena Ortiz: we want: easy onboarding for customers, margins on hosted usage, and clear path to private installs for tier-1 customers
08:42 Maya Chen: alignment — that seems compatible. next steps: we'll send integration brief, capacity questionnaire, and propose dates for technical deep dive. Samir and Olivia will run a quick feasibility run on your GPU profiles once we receive traces
08:56 Diane Xu: timeline: we can aim for pilot kickoff mid-Jan, with a technical deep dive third week of December
09:04 Maya Chen: great. any blockers we haven't covered?
09:07 Rajiv Menon: one more — billing model implications if we resell hosted tier, need consolidated invoices and subaccounting
09:13 Maya Chen: yes, the console supports partner invoicing and subaccount reporting; we'll include a sample billing export in the brief
09:22 Tom Becker: can we also get a sample SLA and an outline of support escalation matrix?
09:28 Maya Chen: yes, will attach.
09:33 Lena Ortiz: okay let's capture action items, and thanks everyone
09:38 Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up.
09:40 -- end of recording --

Notes: transcription contains typical mis-hears, e.g., 'onramp' sometimes transcribed as 'on ramp' and 'KV' spelled out as 'K V' in a few spots. links referenced: Integration brief (to be shared), Pilot workbook (internal link), Security pack (SOC2 + pen-test summaries).
